newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol slips, seen recouping on share offer.
newsitem.headline: Repsol slips, seen recouping on share offer.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Repsol were sharply lower on Thursday on continued profit-taking after a strong rise during this month's privatisation, dealers said.

"The stock's been falling for three days now, but it may be touching bottom. There's been sales from all over the place, but most of those will probably be speculative, with traders taking profits after big gains in the past weeks," said a dealer at ABN-Amro in Madrid.
At 1220 GMT, Repsol was down 50 pesetas, 0.80 percent, to 6,180 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was flat at 5,802.43.
But some dealers are expecting the shares to rise again during Friday and Monday's sessions, with the final price of the share offer to be fixed on Monday.
"I don't think the placement price will be much further away from the share price last Friday, which means it has to rise again before Monday's close," a dealer said.
He said apart from profit-taking by traders, Repsol's weakness in the past few days versus the rest of the market may be an attempt by the sale managers to avoid the final price being too high.

"If Repsol continued at the same rate as the rest of the bourse it would be well over 6,500 pesetas by now, something potential buyers wouldn't like too much," said a dealer at an independent brokerage.

The shares have weakened since a closing high of 6,370 pesetas on April 21, the closing date for provisional orders for the retail tranche of this month's share offer and the day on which the maximum retail price was fixed at 6,327 pesetas.
Analysts expect retail investors to pay between 6,000 and 6,100 pesetas per share, once the four percent discount for that tranche has been applied to Monday's price.
The government is selling its last 10 percent stake in the energy blue chip this month in a share offer which runs until Friday.
Strong demand by the Spanish public for the shares, oversubscribed by around 37 times, has seen the listed shares rocket from 5,820 pesetas on April 3.
"We've seen a lot of traders taking advantage of the fact that the offer managers had been running the price up. They're now taking profits," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage in Madrid.
A comment in the Financial Times' Lex column on Thursday, indicating that international investors may not be too motivated to buy at current levels may have had some impact, dealers said.

"I'd heard that on the international tranche the offer wasn't going as well. But really that shouldn't be a problem seeing as what they'll do will be simply increase the domestic tranche," the dealer added.
Technically, the stock could retrace back to support at 6,040 pesetas, according to a Central Hispano Bolsa dealer.
